current.title: Fabrication of Bicontinuous Cement Composites with Multifunctional Structural and Electrical Properties
current.description: This research focuses on engineering bicontinuous cement-based composites that simultaneously exhibit enhanced mechanical performance and tunable electrical conductivity. The work integrates principles from materials science, electrochemistry, and civil engineering to develop composites suitable for smart structural applications, including structural health monitoring, self-sensing capabilities, and electromagnetic shielding. The study leverages multiscale characterization techniques to understand the interplay between microstructure, connectivity, and multifunctional properties.

previous.title: Blast Load Effects on Building Structures
previous.description: Experimental investigation of boiler blast loads on building structures at BUET. Included large- and small-scale specimen testing, dynamic data acquisition, and assessment of structural resilience. Funded by the CASR grant, BUET.

previous.title: Fiber-Reinforced & Sustainable Concrete
previous.description: Extensive experimental study of mechanical behavior of concrete with natural and synthetic fibers — including jute, PVC, banana, and coconut fibers — and supplementary cementitious materials such as fly ash, rice husk ash, sugarcane bagasse ash (SCBA), and wood powder. Published 6+ peer-reviewed journal papers on these topics.

previous.title: Numerical Modeling of RC Structures
previous.description: Developed and validated numerical models of lateral behavior of masonry-infilled RC frames in OpenSees focusing on sliding failure of infill panels, blast-induced column response using Abaqus, and retrofitting of RC columns under lateral loads. Parametric studies informed design recommendations for retrofitting strategies.
